transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

I guess… I’ve just been feeling like I’m messing things up for people. Not in a dramatic way, I mean, I know everyone makes mistakes, but I keep getting stuck on this feeling that I ruined things or let people down.

Like with my apprenticeship, I keep thinking I’m kind of a fake there, even though I’m trying. And then I feel guilty, like I’m disappointing my family and even the younger apprentices, over stuff other people would probably just fix and move on from. I’m not sure if that makes sense.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things as much as you used to, even things you normally like doing?

Yeah… I mean, a little, I guess. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I’ve noticed I’ll walk right past my sketchbook and not even feel like picking it up. And I’ve skipped volleyball, and I’ll see texts from the volunteer group and just kind of… leave them there.

Those used to be things that made me feel like me, you know? Lately I just don’t feel much about them. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling guilty or like you’re a burden to others more often than usual?

Yeah… more than usual, I think. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m blaming myself for everything, but that’s kind of what made me come in.

I keep getting this feeling that I’ve ruined things for everybody, or that I’m not really good enough to be in the apprenticeship… like I’m sort of faking it and people are going to realize. And then I feel like I’m letting my family down, and even the younger apprentices, over things that I know other people would probably just fix and move on from.

I know that might sound a little over the top. I’m trying not to be dramatic about it, but it’s been sticking with me.
Have you ever had a period where you felt so energetic or wired that you needed less sleep than usual, but still felt rested?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I didn’t really see it as a problem at the time, because I was still getting to work and class and everything.

There was a stretch where I was only sleeping maybe three or four hours, and I’d still show up feeling really wired, like I had plenty of energy. It didn’t feel like I was tired the way I probably should’ve been.

Now it’s kind of the opposite, or just different—I’ll have trouble falling asleep, or I’ll wake up before my alarm and feel like I didn’t actually rest. Does that answer what you mean?
Has there been a time when you completely lost interest in things you usually enjoy, like your sketchbook or volleyball, to the point where you didn’t care about doing them at all?

Yeah… I mean, “completely” feels like a strong word, but it has been kind of like that lately.

I’ll walk past my sketchbook and just… not feel anything about it, even though normally I’d at least want to mess around with something. And I’ve skipped volleyball, and when the volunteer group texts, I kind of just leave it sitting there. Those things used to make me feel like myself, so it’s weird that I don’t really care much right now.

I don’t know if that counts as completely losing interest, but it’s definitely not normal for me.
Have you noticed a change in your energy levels lately, like feeling more tired than usual even when you haven’t done much?

I don’t know… I haven’t really been tracking it that closely. I mean, I get tired sometimes, but I don’t want to overstate it if it’s just normal tired, you know?

I guess lately I’m not as quick to jump into things, but I’m not sure if I’d call it a big energy change. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed that your thoughts have been slower than usual, or that you're moving more slowly, like you're kind of in a fog or everything takes more effort?

Yeah… maybe a little. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, because I’m still doing my job, but I’ve noticed it there more than anywhere.

Like on the job, I’ll catch myself moving slower than usual, like even climbing down to grab a fitting takes more effort than it should. Or if a foreman asks me something, it takes me a second to answer, like my brain has to catch up.

A couple people have asked if I’m sick or hungover, which is embarrassing because I’m not trying to seem like that. So… yeah, I guess that’s kind of what you mean?
Have you been feeling worse about yourself lately, like you’re not good enough or that you’ve let people down more than you actually have?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t love saying it because it sounds kind of self-pitying, but that’s actually a big part of why I came in.

I keep feeling like I’ve ruined things for everybody, even when it’s probably stuff other people would just fix and move on from. Like at work, I start thinking I’m a fake in the apprenticeship, like everyone’s going to figure out I don’t belong there. And then I feel like I’m letting my family down, or even the younger apprentices who kind of look to me sometimes.

I know, logically, it might be bigger in my head than it really is… but it feels really true when I’m in it. Does that make sense?
Can you think of a specific time recently when you felt absolutely no interest or pleasure in something you usually enjoy, like your sketchbook or volleyball, even for a full day or more?

Yeah… I guess so. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m just being lazy or anything, but lately I’ll walk right past my sketchbook and not even feel that little pull to pick it up.

Same with volleyball — I’ve skipped it when normally I’d be glad to go, and it wasn’t like I was busy or had a good reason. And with the volunteer group texts, I’ll see them come in and just… not really care enough to answer.

Those are usually the things that make me feel like myself, so it feels weird to not feel much about them. Is that what you mean?
Can you tell me if there was a time when these feelings—like not enjoying things, feeling guilty, and moving more slowly—lasted for at least two weeks straight without much relief?

Yeah… I think it’s definitely been more than two weeks. I don’t want to overstate it, because there have been days where I can still get through things, but that heavier stretch has kind of been there for… maybe about nine months now.

It got harder to pretend it was fine once school and work started slipping a bit. Before that I kept telling myself I was just tired or needed to get organized, but it hasn’t really fully let up. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you found that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy, like your sketchbook or volleyball, nearly every day for most of the day?

Yeah… most days, I think. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it’s been kind of like I can just walk past my sketchbook and feel nothing about it. Or I’ll skip volleyball and not really miss it the way I normally would.

Even the volunteer group texts — I see them and just don’t answer, not because I’m mad or anything, just… I don’t feel that usual spark. Those things used to make me feel like me, so it feels a little weird to admit. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
